lead: Digital signage introduces a changing content system rather than a single printed message. A screen may present menus, directions or promotional information, but its usefulness depends on who maintains the content and how the hardware fits the site. For a New York project, begin by defining the audience, viewing conditions and update routine. This page is a planning draft for discussion with Vision Graphics; equipment supply, software, electrical work, support and installation are not represented as confirmed services until the project offering is reviewed.

sections.html: Identify who writes, approves and changes the messages. Decide what must remain visible and what can rotate. A readable menu and a fast-moving promotional loop have different layout needs. Consider a fallback for essential information when a screen or connection is unavailable.

sections.h2: Define the hardware and service questions
sections.html: Document viewing distance, ambient light, indoor or outdoor placement, connectivity and access. Hardware selection, mounting, power and any software subscriptions need a verified specification. Confirm ongoing support responsibilities and costs before treating a display concept as a complete signage solution.

items.p: Organize changing items and prices with a readable content hierarchy.
Explore directories or announcements where a screen serves a defined audience.
Plan short messages with an approved update and review routine.

items.q: Does VG provide digital hardware and software?
items.a_html: That offering must be confirmed. This draft does not promise equipment, subscriptions, integrations or support.

items.q: What is needed before choosing a screen?
items.a_html: Define the content, viewing conditions, mounting location, update responsibility and technical support requirements first.
